openings: Can Playback work with our setup? We have a USB-C iPad on supported iPadOS, Playback Premium, a Focusrite 4i4, an official Apple USB-C adapter and a powered USB hub. We want click and guide separately plus stereo music.

Before rehearsal, can you check whether our gear is a documented fit? It's a USB-C iPad with Premium, a Focusrite 4i4 connected through the Apple adapter and powered hub. We need separate click, separate guide and a stereo track feed.

reviewOnly.facts: The official tested-device list names Focusrite 4i4, four outputs, USB hub required. Goal is compatibility advice, not hardware configuration or purchase.
reviewOnly.expected: Retrieve applicable requirements; confirm documented arrangement with relevant conditions without unsupported end-to-end guarantees or unnecessary escalation.

turns.input: Before rehearsal, can you check whether our gear is a documented fit? It's a USB-C iPad with Premium, a Focusrite 4i4 connected through the Apple adapter and powered hub. We need separate click, separate guide and a stereo track feed.
turns.reply:
Let me check the documentation on that.

Yes—your USB-C iPad, Apple USB-C AV adapter, powered hub, and Focusrite 4i4 are a documented setup; the 4i4 requires the powered hub. With Premium, Playback MultiOuts can provide separate click, guide, and a stereo tracks bus across the 4 interface outputs.

results.title: Playback Supported Audio Interfaces (multitracks.com)
results.summary: The tested-and-confirmed interface list, with output counts and whether a USB hub is required: PlayAUDIO12 (10 outputs, setup required, MIDI USB/Ethernet), iConnectAUDIO4c (6), Behringer U-PHORIA UMC1820 (10, setup required), TASCAM 20x20 (10), TASCAM Series 208i (8, setup required), TASCAM 16x08 (8), MOTU Ultralite AVB (10, setup required), Behringer X32/M32 digital mixer (10, setup required), Behringer U-PHORIA UMC404HD (4, setup required, REQUIRES USB hub), Focusrite 4i4 (4, REQUIRES USB hub), Dante AVIO USB Adapter (2, setup required), PreSonus iTwo (2, REQUIRES USB hub), ART USB Stereo DI (2). None of them charge the iPad/iPhone. The page does not separate iOS from Mac and names no Ethernet adapters other than the AVIO.

steps.text: If the caller's interface is on this list and marked 'requires USB hub' (UMC404HD, Focusrite 4i4, PreSonus iTwo), it must be connected through a powered USB hub.
Interfaces marked 'setup required' need configuration on the interface itself (see the interface's own article, e.g. the X32/M32 or U-PHORIA articles) before Playback can send multiple outputs.
An interface not on this list is not necessarily unsupported: the docs say Playback is generally compatible with class-compliant USB interfaces, but it has not been tested by MultiTracks.

results.title: How to Use Playback with Your Sound System
results.summary: Three documented ways to get audio out of Playback: the built-in headphone port with Auto-Pan (2 channels: click/guide left, tracks right), a USB audio interface (up to 32 outputs, grouped into mono or stereo buses), and networked audio such as Dante or SoundGrid (iPad/iPhone limited to two channels; macOS can route up to 32 via Dante Virtual Soundcard). Bluetooth, subscription tiers, and menu paths are not covered here.

steps.text: Option 1 - headphone port: Auto-Pan is on by default. Use a 1/8" TRS to dual 1/4" TS cable, a stereo DI (or two mono DIs) to convert to XLR, then XLR to the stage box. Devices without a headphone jack can use a Lightning-to-3.5mm or USB-C-to-3.5mm adapter. Left channel feeds in-ears (click/guide); right feeds the house mix.

Option 2 - USB audio interface: up to 32 outputs via a supported class-compliant interface. Lightning devices need an Apple Lightning Digital AV Adapter; USB-C devices need an Apple USB-C Digital AV Multiport Adapter. Add a powered USB hub if the interface is bus-powered. Outputs are grouped into custom buses, mono or stereo.

Option 3 - networked audio (Dante, SoundGrid): connect the Playback device to a network running that protocol. iPad and iPhone support only two channels over networked audio; macOS apps like Dante Virtual Soundcard can route up to 32 channels.
Use an in-ear monitoring solution so click and guide are not heard by the congregation. Accompaniment tracks do not include click and guide.

results.title: How do I connect my USB audio interface to Playback?
results.summary: iOS-focused guide for connecting a USB audio interface, directly via an official Apple adapter or through a powered USB hub (required when also using a MIDI controller or Ethernet MIDI). Playback recognizes the interface as its audio device once connected. The article states Playback sends up to 10 individual outputs with instrument tracks routed to 10 buses; note that other articles (Track & Bus Routing, Sound System) cite 16 buses and up to 32 outputs, so this figure may be dated.

steps.text: Direct: connect the iOS device to an approved interface with an official Apple adapter (Lightning: Apple USB 3 to Lightning camera adapter; USB-C: Apple USB-C AV adapter). These allow charging while connected.

Via powered hub: connect the hub to the device with the Apple adapter, then connect the interface to the hub. Playback recognizes the interface as its audio device. Hubs the article confirms: 7-port Anker (1 charge port), 7-port Plugable (2 charge ports), 7-port StarTech.
Keep USB runs short: 16 ft max (USB 2.0), 3 m / 9 ft max (USB 3.0). Powered extenders: repeater needs external power; 25 m (USB 2.0) / 15 m (USB 3.0) max.
Hub must be powered and have no more than 7 accessory ports.
Further problems: see Troubleshooting Playback Audio Issues.

results.text:
- Auto-Pan: When enabled, Auto Pan routes the click & guide through the left and all tracks through the right outputs of the iOS device’s stereo output. results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Setting up Audio and MIDI
results.text:
There are two main ways to send audio out of Playback.

· Auto Pan: Send click and tracks from Playback using the headphone port without any additional audio hardware. Learn how to use Auto Pan with Playback.

· MultiOuts: With a Premium subscription, Playback can send up to 32 outputs can be accessed using compatible audio devices.

Note: For more info on audio routing see:
- 📖Setting up Playback with a sound system
- 📖Connecting to a USB Interface
- 📖Troubleshooting Playback Audio Issues

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > General Settings Tab
results.text:
- Metronome Style VU: Enable the Click volume meters to flash like a metronome (enabled) or reflect the real-time volume output (disabled)
- Song Specific Master Fader: When enabled, each song has a separate master fader volume. Disable for a global master fader volume across every song.
- Fader Default Level at 80%: When enabled, a song is added to Playback with all faders preset at 80%. This provides headroom for increasing track volumes if needed. Disable to load a song with all track faders at 100% volume.
- Power Saver: Enable to improve performance on older devices and decrease battery consumption. Power Saver disables fader VU meters, Fader multi-touch, and reduces waveform scrolling feedback.
- MIDI Out: Enables the MIDI Out engine by default. Disable if not using MIDI Out; this will improve Playback performance and decrease battery consumption.
